title: Why did A Good Person (2023) have to veer so sharply into melodrama in the third act?

commenti.body:
>Or is it an example of a relatively inexperienced, but naturally talented, filmmaker running out of steam?

Caveat--I haven't seen it yet.

However--3rd act problems are almost always a script problem. I'll use "Hancock" as an example--this was a really interesting film that turned the superhero trope on its ear, and then it turns into a domestic drama. That's entirely 100% on the script.
